english: Let $F:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $F'(x)=\dfrac{1}{x+\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}}$ for all $x>0$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^{+}}F(x)=0$. Then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(F(x)-\dfrac12\log_{e}x\right)$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $F:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए सभी $x>0$ के लिए $F'(x)=\dfrac{1}{x+\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}}$ तथा $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^{+}}F(x)=0$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(F(x)-\dfrac12\log_{e}x\right)$ बराबर है
solution_full: Use the Euler substitution $\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}=t-x$ (with $t=x+\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}>0$). Squaring: $x^{2}+2x=t^{2}-2tx+x^{2}$, so $x=\dfrac{t^{2}}{2(t+1)}$.
As $x\to0^{+}$ both terms tend to $0$, so $C=0$.
Also $\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}-x=\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}+x}\to1$, so the second term tends to $\dfrac12$.
The limit is $\dfrac{1+\log_{e}2}{2}$. Option (B) drops the algebraic term and (C) has its sign reversed.
originality_note: New: the antiderivative of 1/(x + sqrt(x^2+2x)) is normalised at 0 and its logarithmic growth is subtracted at infinity, so the answer is the constant left in its asymptotic expansion (way 2). Closest known: Euler substitution exercises for 1/(x + sqrt(x^2+ax+b)). Different because: the question asks for the finite part of the antiderivative at infinity, so both the log term and the algebraic term must be found and their limits taken.
key_step: Euler substitution sqrt(x^2+2x) = t - x turning the integrand into a rational function, then the asymptotics of both terms.
justification: An Euler substitution is less practised than standard forms (F1), followed by a limit that needs both parts of the antiderivative. Two linked ideas with options to check; comparable to 2025-P2-Q1 (L2) and 2023-P2-Q8 (L3), placed at L3.
blueprint_concepts: Euler and reciprocal substitutions for irrational integrands

concept_use.Euler and reciprocal substitutions for i: The substitution sqrt(x^2+2x) = t - x makes the integrand rational: (t+2)/(2(t+1)^2) dt.
concept_use.Integration of irrational algebraic func: The irrational integrand 1/(x + sqrt(x^2+2x)) is integrated and written back in x, with 1/(t+1) rationalised to x + 1 - sqrt(x^2+2x).
